newsitem.title: MEXICO: Germany's Kohl sits in New Beetle.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Kohl sits in New Beetle.

text.p: Any worries about leg-room in the car destined to replace Volkswagen's famous, but tiny, Beetle were put to rest on Friday by German Chancellor Helmut Kohl.

After unveiling the first prototype of the New Beetle, built at the German carmakers' giant plant just outside this central Mexican city, the portly German leader glided effortlessly into the front passenger seat.
Joining Kohl in the car's driver seat was the trim Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo.
"As you can see, the car is plenty big enough," joked Volkswagen's North American chief Jens Newman.
The white, oval-shaped car is the first of what Volkswagen hopes will be millions of New Beetles to be made here and shipped to the rest of the world.

Sleeker, sturdier and more powerful than its predecessor, the New Beetle is intended to offer a modern alternative to carowners who still think fondly of the original Bug-shaped sedan. Along with the innovations comes a heftier price tag, however -- about $12,000 to $13,000.
"For a German of my generation, the Beetle is not just any car," Kohl said. "I got my first drivers' license in a Beetle."
As the only remaining producer of the Beetle, Puebla's plant was picked by Volkswagen as the logical place to begin making the heir to arguably the world's most popular car.

Volkswagen plans to spend $500 million in the next two years revamping its Puebla plant to begin producing the car by late 1997 and selling it by early 1998. The factory will eventually produce 120,000 New Beetles a year.

In return for long-term supply contracts, Volkswagens' suppliers, mostly German-based companies such as Siemens and Bosch, will spend another $500 million in outfitting their nearby supply facilities.
Zedillo said plans to build the New Beetle in Mexico were a sign of Germany's confidence in the country's sometimes volatile economy.
To mark the occasion, Volkswagen rolled the 21,300,000th Beetle off the production belt.
